speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a pruritic rash on both upper arms; tell me, how long has this rash been present, and have you noticed any specific triggers like new soaps, plants, or insect bites?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. She denies any recent illnesses and mentions that she has not started any new medications or come into contact with any new substances that she is aware of.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Atopic dermatitis (eczema). The chronic nature of the rash, its location on the extremities, the intense itch, and the lack of response to simple avoidance measures strongly suggest an atopic diathesis. I will proceed with examining the skin morphology to confirm the diagnosis.
